Hi Jeff,

I'm Hal, the technical specialist at HeliumDeploy. You're right to be fed up. You asked a clear question in October and kept getting the same line back with no one answering it. I've now sent the swap and return shipping question to the two people who run the business. They'll pick up your ticket and answer you by email. I've sent the overheating to JD, our hardware lead, along with everything you've told me.

On the miner: a 68°F room is a normal place to run a B30. Three chips on one board overheating within five minutes is not normal, and you shouldn't just live with it. When chips on one board run hot and the other board stays cool, the room is usually not the cause. It usually means a fan problem or poor contact between those chips and the heatsink.

A few checks will show which it is. Please leave the case closed while you do them:

1. Make sure the fans are spinning and look at the fan speed readings in the dashboard. If one fan is much slower or reads zero, that's the answer.
2. Set the fans to 100% (or auto) and switch to the lowest power mode your firmware offers. Then leave about 6 inches of clear space at the front and back of the unit, and keep it out of any cabinet or enclosure.
3. Let it run for 15 minutes. Then take a screenshot of the dashboard showing the chip temperatures on both boards and the fan speeds.

Please also reply with:

1. The firmware version from the dashboard
2. The mode you were on when it overheated
3. A short phone video of the unit running when the overheat happens
4. A clear photo of the serial number label

If those three chips still run hot at full fan in the lowest mode while the other board stays cool, that's a fault on that board, not the room. JD can then make a quick call on it. If you want a faster answer, the Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf is quickest. Mention @nullhashrate (that's JD) and post the screenshot there too.

Hal
